## Section 56 — restart transaction settlement, Android return-gate dedup, prepared reservation consume/read owners, and publication cache/lifecycle focused oracles

### 56.1 Restart coordinator settlement and superseded-reload oracles

- `src/gateway/server-reload-restart.ts@0928715f2a790d917c38860dc45253352d1abb08` is the direct restart-coordinator state owner below Section 55's hot-reload recovery path. Its single `GatewayRestartTransaction` keeps the current lifecycle/request operation in `pending|committed|rejected`, owns one restart deferral, and fences every delayed preflight/emission by exact operation identity plus scheduler/reload signals. A stopped coordinator returns `recovery-pending` instead of silently accepting a restart; a superseding config/request cancels the predecessor deferral and retires a rejected operation; a failed preparation or failed recovery emission settles that exact operation rejected; and a stale preflight cannot emit after a newer request becomes current.
- `src/gateway/server-reload-contracts.ts@3a997626bce777b1c36a7432b69527f25117a2c2` makes that settlement contract explicit: restart transactions expose `accepted|recovery-pending` admission and a one-way settlement from pending into committed or rejected, while request options carry the runtime-config preparation hook used by the coordinator.
- `src/gateway/server-reload-managed.ts@3e15ee0f3454023c6a8c4c57d0c3cad63932a49c` is the next production caller/transaction bridge. It begins the restart lifecycle before managed config replacement, pauses it for a candidate, asks the coordinator to restart with prepared runtime config, rejects `recovery-pending` as a `GatewayHotReloadRecoveryError`, settles both request and lifecycle committed only after accepted restart handling, and settles both rejected plus rolls back runtime environment on failure. It publishes deferred applied-config hashes only after candidate settlement, so a newer config cannot inherit predecessor restart debt.
- `src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts@25dc76bbafd25b9e8fc42533532f2128cce96f08` is the focused supersession/settlement oracle. It proves rejected preflight/lifecycle debt is retired when a newer config is accepted; restart emission failure is reported without an automatic retry; managed shutdown joins already-admitted config restart completion/AbortError; delayed channel failure after restart handling stops cannot schedule post-commit recovery; a held old preflight is revalidated and cannot signal after an explicit reapply; and a newer valid restart config replaces the deferred restart owner without stale side effects.

## Section 66 — transferred native-root receivers, retained chat-panel retirement, and retained Gateway authority handoff

Frozen upstream remains `openclaw/openclaw@ad8d12f126d29b0db204187adf5092db80294e70`. This section continues only the three Section 65 frontiers requested for this pass. Section 64/65 already own the `GatewayClientRegistry`, authenticated WebSocket dispatcher, recycled-connId transport, primary-window, retained page, and initial native-root lease rows; those exact refs remain anchors and are not re-counted here.

### 66.1 Worker-transferred native roots terminate in admission custody, not worker generation custody

- New production exact-ref `src/plugins/plugin-generation-preparation.worker.ts@22055912ec8cfadd3ccaeaffd5298bc0056ab260` is the preparation-isolate side of the transfer. `admissionChanges()` selects only changed receipts/publications, retains each referenced native root before encoding it, then removes a publication intent from the worker state only after that intent and its native custody have been handed to the host-side admission owner. A worker-created native-root object is only a borrowed host reference: its local commit/dispose methods are no-ops, and the codec refuses to import a native-root lease into the preparation isolate. Worker close first settles native admissions and joins all owned resources, so source execution retirement is not allowed to substitute for native-admission settlement.
- New production exact-ref `src/plugins/plugin-generation-worker-codec.ts@1d4551251dd8e4488f1cbbcd089799a6b2fe6fef` is the concrete receiver boundary. Encoding a native-root descriptor snapshots a temporary lease, exports its root id and immediately releases that sender-side temporary lease; decoding imports a fresh receiver lease. Resource proxies bind remote disposal to receiver-side native-recovery disposal in both sync and async paths, preserving a cleanup failure for retry instead of silently consuming custody. Ordinary released RPC handles are retired separately through `releaseReceivedHandles`, so callable identity lifetime and native-byte lifetime are not conflated.
- New focused oracle `src/plugins/plugin-generation-worker-codec.test.ts@b1bae537efb5739ab5fa5653aa156657c63cb7b0` proves a transferred native root remains alive after the outer recovered object is disposed when a fork still owns it; a nested child/fork can continue using that root and physical disposal occurs exactly once only after the last recovery owner releases it. The same file also proves failed disposal retains the remaining shared callback owner rather than turning a failed cleanup into a false release.
- New production exact-ref `src/plugins/plugin-native-admission.ts@8f7e2e9d1e6e69152ef6a7f748b55915de3ec2b7` is the receiver's recovery owner. Restored recovery snapshots establish owner sets for transferred roots; every recovery, fork, cache-retain and exported recovery snapshot acquires its own root ownership. `dispose` and `disposeAsync` are idempotent and physically retire only roots whose owner set becomes empty. A disposed recovery cannot fork or be snapshotted again, preventing a retired generation from minting fresh native custody.
- New production exact-ref `src/plugins/plugin-native-admission-state.ts@ba6313894f34788a37545d124a79e9916cf37665` adopts a worker transfer into the original admission view with an independent state owner. Publication commits roots only after the current publication is positively accepted; state disposal waits pending publication work, respects borrowers, releases captured-path pins, removes its ownership from each root and asynchronously retires only roots with no remaining owners. An invalidated cache therefore starts a new admission snapshot without letting old-generation cleanup delete still-borrowed bytes.
- New focused stale-generation oracle `src/gateway/server-plugin-reload-recovery.test.ts@a00fed65c48f13e22d0f0e684260c6ba1b42aaf8` deletes the previous worker-backed plugin's captured source before reload. Recovery explicitly marks that plugin unavailable for rollback, emits the missing-capture warning, and then admits the newly edited replacement into a new cache; it does not silently reuse or resurrect the missing old generation. This closes the requested stale-generation/native-retirement layer below the Section 65 host-root lease tests.

### 66.2 Retained chat panes hand observation to current panel/detail surfaces and retire on reconnect or disposal

- New production exact-ref `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-page-retained-sessions.ts@b7c14329215d57db49d2aae7115971560d350487` is the retained-pane membership/eviction owner under Section 65's page state. Fixed slots preserve surviving pane instances while ordinary navigation evicts only panes without queued edits; explicit `discardPane` first discards every mounted staged attachment presentation, then clears pane/session handoff state before deleting retention. A later disconnect therefore cannot restage payloads under a reused pane id. By contrast page disconnect itself is non-terminal and only clears page tracking/listeners so a legitimate remount can recover staged composer custody.
- New production exact-ref `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-lifecycle.ts@800a0982e7fa72df0fc3f305d208e6c8571dceab` is the mounted retained-pane lifetime. Only active+presented panes own shortcut/native-draft input and panel actions; every Gateway edge synchronously re-applies connection ownership before presentation work proceeds. Disposal retires active resources, companion/composer presentation, model recovery, metadata/initial transcript requests, deferred hydration, PR/task/suggestion/reaction/typing state and swarm hydration, then increments `connectionGeneration`, clears the connected client and destroys the page state. Staged attachments are either explicitly discarded or handed off according to the pane's terminal-close flag, so DOM disconnect cannot become a second composer writer.
- New production exact-ref `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-session-panel.tsx@172e5c339c43ea884267410ed3c6896db4e15682` is the generic session-panel observation consumer. Its identity is the current `[sessionKey, agentId]`; when presentation disappears or that identity changes it immediately calls the existing data owner with `presented:false` to retire old reads, then admits only the final related host inputs in one queued microtask. Unmount deletes the input handler and disposes both projection and data owner, so a replaced Solid surface cannot keep polling/mutation authority.
- New direct details consumer `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-details-session.tsx@a61daace02fd7b2a75f1497ba3252e2a68e1d5d9` keeps one shared `ProcessesPanelData` owner at the native details host across keyed detail replacements. Its panel identity follows session+agent, while detail identity also includes selected session id; bridge property changes synchronously call `syncSessionPanelInputs`. ### 76.1 Cache retirement is a production cleanup owner for pending or unaccepted native-admission publication

- New production exact-ref `src/plugins/plugin-cache.ts@49cd64897c3fa5f7387514c829a48043a2e0381b` closes a cleanup ownership edge that the prior sections had only reached through admission-state/root owners. `retirePluginCache` installs one retirement promise, quiesces setup/instance resources, waits registry and instance cleanup, then takes custody of `cache.sourceAdmissions`. If an instance drain timed out, native-admission disposal is deferred until those bounded-retirement settlement promises finish; otherwise retirement awaits `nativeAdmissions.dispose()` inline. Cleanup failure is surfaced as `Plugin native capture cleanup failed` rather than silently dropping the ownership.
- The already registered `plugin-native-admission-state.ts@ba6313894f34788a37545d124a79e9916cf37665` defines what that disposal means: it waits current publication work, removes the retiring cache borrower, explicitly settles queued publications once more, releases capture pins, removes state ownership from native roots and physically disposes only roots with no remaining owners. A publisher that returns `false` or throws does not commit/delete the queued publication intent; retirement therefore remains the production boundary that eventually releases the admission-owned native custody when the cache generation goes away.
- This is more direct than Section 75's later orphan sweep: the orphan reconciler reasons from durable receipts after the fact, while cache retirement owns the in-memory admission/pending-publication lifetime itself. It still is not a special failed-publication callback: there is no separate receiver invoked with one failed publication result. Failure/unaccepted publication remains represented by the admission state, and cache retirement disposes that state.
